claims.claim: WTI front-month crude price and change
Oil recovered from its low, calculated ($92.72 less $91.51)
Iran's stated timetable to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, stated by foreign minister Abbas Araghchi at the UN General Assembly
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio cautioned against calling the meeting a breakthrough
White House said talks with mediators are positive and constructive

stories.dek: Shares are up again and the reason is cheaper oil. Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi told a gathering at the UN in New York that the Strait of Hormuz — the shipping lane that carries the Gulf's oil exports — would reopen on the seventh day if Washington lifts its naval blockade, waives sanctions on Iranian oil and holds a ceasefire. US oil fell to $92.72, down 2.00%. But Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to call it a breakthrough, and oil has already handed back $1.21 of its fall. Cheaper energy helps almost every company's costs. Watch whether either government puts this in writing.
stories.headline: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz in seven days and oil falls
stories.short: Iran offers Hormuz reopening; oil falls, shares rise

claims.claim: Distance to the 30 buy-window level, calculated (30 less 14.84)

stories.dek: The VIX, the market's fear gauge, is at 14.84, down 5.29% on the day and its lowest reading of the session. Anything under 15 counts as calm; 15 to 20 is normal, 20 to 30 nervous, and above 30 is where the BuyTrigger system treats a sell-off as a buying window. At 14.84 the gauge sits 15.16 points below that line. In plain terms, insurance against a fall is the cheapest it has been all day, which is what a quiet market looks like rather than a bargain. Watch for the gauge to rise, not fall, if you are waiting for the window.
stories.headline: The fear gauge drops under 15, its calmest level all day
stories.short: Fear gauge at 14.84 — calm, not a buying window

claims.claim: Amount above Thursday's session high, calculated ($1,083.48 less $1,081.04)
Micron fiscal Q4 results date, company-confirmed

stories.dek: Micron ($MU) is at $1,083.48, up 0.27%, and for the first time this week it is above both Thursday's closing price of $1,080.53 and Thursday's intraday high of $1,081.04 — $2.44 above it. Seven times this week the shares have opened higher after hours and failed to hold it by the close; this is the eighth attempt, with half an hour of trading left. Micron makes the memory chips that AI data centres consume, so the pattern matters for the whole chain. The real test is the company's own results, due Wednesday 30 September at 21:30 UK.
stories.headline: Micron finally trades above where it closed on Thursday
stories.short: Micron tops Thursday's close after seven failed tries

claims.claim: Bloom Energy change on the same news

stories.dek: Oracle ($ORCL) is at $137.50, down 1.46%, and it has slipped a little further with each check through the afternoon, touching a low of $137.06. The cause is a delay to Project Jupiter, the giant data centre Oracle is having built, where a force majeure notice has pushed back the power supply. The contrast with its fuel-cell supplier Bloom Energy, up almost 9% on the same news, is the lesson: when a project slips, the customer wears the delay and the supplier that bridges it gets paid. Watch for a formal filing from either side rather than more statements to reporters.
stories.headline: Oracle keeps falling as its data centre delay is priced in
stories.short: Oracle down 1.46% as the power delay keeps biting

claims.claim: Bloom Energy share price and change
Bloom Energy newest SEC filing date (CIK 1664703), acceptance 2026-09-18T22:50:15Z
Oracle newest SEC filing date (CIK 1341439), acceptance 2026-09-23T23:22:27Z
Project Jupiter fuel-cell contract size, as Bloom stated to the press

stories.dek: Bloom Energy ($BE) is at $290.44, up 8.92%, a second day of sharp gains after it told reporters that Oracle remains committed to their 2.4 gigawatt fuel-cell contract on the original timeline. What is missing is paperwork. I checked the US regulator's filing index this afternoon: Bloom's most recent filing of any kind is dated 18 September and Oracle's 23 September, so neither company has filed anything about the reaffirmation. A statement to the press is not a contract disclosure. If an 8-K arrives from Bloom, Oracle or their financing partner Blue Owl, the story gets firmer ground under it.
stories.headline: Bloom Energy's 9% jump still rests on a press statement
stories.short: Bloom up 8.9% with no filing behind it

claims.claim: Nvidia trading range width, calculated ($226.94 less $223.13)

stories.dek: Nvidia ($NVDA) is at $224.06, down 0.23%, having crossed back and forth over the flat line three times through the session. Nothing has come out of the company; the shares have simply drifted inside a $3.81 trading range. For anyone holding for years this is worth naming precisely because it means nothing — a share that wanders either side of unchanged on no information is not telling you anything about the business. The real signals for the AI chain this week sit elsewhere: Micron's results next Wednesday and the Oracle data centre delay.
stories.headline: Nvidia changes direction a third time today on no news
stories.short: Nvidia flips a third time, down 0.23%

claims.claim: 10-year Treasury par yield, most recent published row
No 25 September row served in the daily Treasury yield curve table when read this run
Ten-year yield reported near 5.2% intraday by market commentary, not an official level

stories.dek: The US Treasury had not published Friday's yield figures when I checked at 19:33 UTC, so the most recent official reading for the ten-year government bond is still 5.18%, from Thursday 24 September. That matters because long-term interest rates set the discount on every future profit a company earns, and 5.18% is the highest this figure has been in years. Market commentary through the afternoon put it near 5.2% intraday, but that is a reported estimate, not the official number, so it is not used here. Treasury normally publishes after the New York close.
stories.headline: No official US interest rate reading published for today yet
stories.short: Still no official Treasury figure for Friday
